stem: A logistics team wants a first working tool: shipment records from a carrier system and a warehouse list from a database must become one view where dispatchers can reassign late shipments. Which sequence matches the end-to-end path in Foundry?

choices.text: Map the raw source tables straight into one object type per source system, then let each dispatcher clean the data in the app before acting on it
Build the Workshop screens first, then define object types to match the screens, and connect the source systems last once users approve the layout
Bring both sources in as datasets, clean and combine them in a pipeline, map the result to object types and links, then build a Workshop app with an Action
Export both sources to spreadsheets, combine them by hand once a week, upload the combined file, and share it with dispatchers as a read-only dataset

stem: A new builder asks what Pipeline Builder is for in the end-to-end workflow and whether people who do not write code can use it. Which description matches the documentation?

choices.text: It is the connector catalog used to authenticate to external systems, and it has no transform features beyond copying source tables unchanged
It is a monitoring console that only reports build failures; the transformation logic itself must always be written in Code Repositories by engineers
It is a dashboard builder for end users that charts raw datasets directly, so it replaces the need to create object types or operational applications
It is the main data integration application, where coders and non-coders build pipelines that turn raw sources into clean outputs through a graph interface

stem: A team has clean shipment and warehouse datasets and wants dispatchers to act on them in an application. A colleague asks why the datasets should be mapped into object types first. Which reason fits the docs?

choices.text: Object types are required only for storage quotas; they hold a compressed copy of the dataset so that builds finish faster than with plain tables
Object types turn rows and columns into real-world concepts with links and actions, which Workshop uses to read data and to capture user decisions
Object types are a reporting format for exporting data to external BI tools, and Workshop can read datasets equally well without them
Object types replace the datasets entirely, so the pipeline can be deleted once the objects exist and no further builds will be needed

stem: A builder combines two carrier files into one shipments table with a union in Pipeline Builder. One carrier names its column ship_id and the other shipment_id, and the union shows an error. What is the most direct fix?

choices.text: Rename or cast columns in one input so both share the same schema before the union, since a union requires matching schemas
Build the pipeline anyway and let the object type ignore the missing column, since schema errors are only warnings at build time
Replace the union with a join on the carrier name, since a join accepts inputs whose column names do not match and keeps all rows
Write a user-defined function in Java to append the files, since built-in transforms cannot handle tables from different carriers

stem: Each shipment row carries a warehouse_id, and a separate warehouse table holds the warehouse name and region for each id. The team wants every shipment row to show its warehouse name and region. Which Pipeline Builder transform fits?

choices.text: A filter on the warehouse table, which keeps only the warehouses that appear in today's shipments and drops every other row
A join of shipments to warehouses on warehouse_id, which adds the matching warehouse columns to each shipment row
A split of the shipments table on warehouse_id, which sends rows with a known warehouse to one output and the rest to another
A union of the shipment and warehouse tables, which stacks all rows from both inputs into one longer table with a shared schema

stem: A pipeline produces one cleaned shipments table, but domestic and international shipments must go to two different outputs because they back different review processes. Which built-in transform does this in one step?

choices.text: A split, which sends rows that meet a condition to a True output and all remaining rows to a False output
A union, which takes the cleaned table and a copy of it and keeps only the rows that differ between the two copies
A join, which matches the table against a country list and writes unmatched rows to a separate dataset automatically
A pivot, which turns the country column into separate columns, one for domestic values and one for international values

stem: After cleaning shipment and warehouse data in Pipeline Builder, a builder wants the Shipment and Warehouse object types and the link between them without switching tools. What does the documentation support?

choices.text: Pipeline Builder only writes datasets; object types and links can be created only afterwards by an administrator in a separate request process
Create a time series sync output for each table, since time series outputs are the only Ontology outputs Pipeline Builder supports
Add object type and link type outputs in the same pipeline, so the clean data defines the Ontology elements in one workflow
Export the cleaned data to a spreadsheet and import it into Workshop, which creates object types automatically from any uploaded table

stem: A builder adds a Shipment object type output to a pipeline and wants to add a link type output to Driver, but there is nothing to link to. Driver data exists only as a cleaned dataset in the same pipeline. What is missing?

choices.text: A schedule on the pipeline, since link types appear only after the pipeline has run on a recurring basis at least once
A union of the Shipment and Driver tables, since links are created by stacking both tables into one combined output first
A link type can only be created after the app is published, because links are derived from how users navigate between Workshop pages
A Driver object type output in the pipeline, since a link type output defines a relationship between two object type outputs

stem: Dispatchers report that some shipments appear twice in their app. The pipeline that backs the Shipment object type receives occasional duplicate shipment ids from a carrier. Which change stops bad data from reaching the objects?

choices.text: Deduplicate on the shipment id in the pipeline and add a primary key data expectation to the output, so a build with duplicates fails
Remove the Shipment object type and give dispatchers direct access to the raw carrier dataset, which shows the true number of rows
Increase the pipeline's build frequency to every five minutes so that duplicates are overwritten more quickly by later builds
Ask dispatchers to ignore the second copy of any shipment and report duplicates by email so the carrier can correct them at the source

stem: A pipeline build failed overnight and the app still shows yesterday's shipments. The job details show a row count expectation on the output failed because the input arrived nearly empty. What is the right first response?

choices.text: Delete the row count expectation so tomorrow's build succeeds, since an app with fresh data is always better than an app with older data
Check the input source for the incomplete delivery and rerun once it is complete, since the expectation stopped a near-empty build as designed
Grant every dispatcher edit access on the pipeline so they can rerun the build themselves whenever their app shows old data
Rebuild the object type from scratch with a new primary key, since a failed expectation means the Ontology definition is corrupted

stem: The shipments pipeline already feeds a Workshop app in daily use. A builder wants to try a new cleaning rule without risking the data dispatchers see. What is the safest way to work?

choices.text: Pause all builds on the pipeline until the new rule is final, so the app keeps its current data while the builder experiments on main
Edit the main pipeline directly during quiet hours and revert the change from memory if dispatchers report a problem the next morning
Create a branch of the pipeline, change and preview the rule there, then propose merging it into main once the result looks right
Copy every dataset into a personal folder, build a second app for testing, and ask dispatchers to switch apps while testing runs

stem: Main is protected so changes need a proposal and one approval. A builder asks a teammate who helped edit the branch to approve the proposal, but the teammate cannot approve it. Why?

choices.text: Approvals can be given only by platform administrators, so no member of the project team can ever approve a pipeline proposal
The teammate must first archive the branch, since only archived branches can be reviewed and approved for merging into main
Proposals are approved automatically after a fixed waiting period, so manual approvals are blocked until that period ends
A valid approver must have Edit permission on the pipeline and must not have contributed to the proposed change

stem: The carrier sync lands new shipment data every morning, but the dispatchers' app still shows last week's shipments. The pipeline was built once by hand when it was created. What is the most likely gap?

choices.text: The object type has too many properties, so Foundry delays updates to it until a weekly maintenance window runs in the background
The pipeline has no schedule, so its outputs and the objects they back are never rebuilt when new input data arrives
Workshop caches each object for seven days by default, so the dispatchers must clear their browsers to see newly synced shipments
The carrier sync writes to a different branch each day, so the pipeline always reads the oldest branch that exists in the project

stem: A builder adds a filter and a new calculated column to a pipeline and wants to confirm the result looks right before spending compute on a full build. What fits the Pipeline Builder workflow?

choices.text: Build the outputs straight away and inspect the objects in the app, since there is no way to view a transform's result before a build
Export the input dataset to a local spreadsheet, repeat the filter by hand, and compare the totals with yesterday's app data
Ask an engineer to rewrite the transforms in code, since only code transforms can be tested before they run in production
Preview the output after applying the transforms, then build the outputs once the previewed rows and columns look correct

stem: A builder adds three transforms to tidy a delivery-notes column, previews them successfully, and builds. The output dataset is unchanged. The new path ends at the last transform node. What explains it?

choices.text: Pipeline Builder ignores any transform added after the first build, so the pipeline must be recreated to include new logic
Text columns cannot be transformed in Pipeline Builder, so the build silently skips any transform that touches a string column
The new path is not connected to an output, and Pipeline Builder prunes transform paths that do not lead to outputs from builds
Previews always run on a branch, so anything previewed is discarded and must be entered again on main before it is built

stem: Dispatchers type free-text delay reasons such as "truck broke down near depot". The team wants each reason sorted into a few categories inside the pipeline that backs the app, and wants confidence before rollout. What fits?

choices.text: Use an LLM transform in Pipeline Builder to classify the reasons and test it with the LLM evaluation suite before deploying it
Send the full notes table to a public chatbot each night, paste the answers into a spreadsheet, and upload it as a new dataset
Train a custom model from scratch on all historic notes before any categories are produced, since pipelines cannot call language models
Leave the text as entered and ask each dispatcher to pick the category later in the app, since pipelines cannot interpret free text

stem: A builder needs to standardize date formats and trim spaces across a carrier table and is considering a custom Python user-defined function for it. What does the guidance recommend?

choices.text: Move the whole pipeline to a spreadsheet tool, since date cleaning and trimming are not supported in any Foundry pipeline
Always write user-defined functions first, since custom code is faster and easier to maintain than any built-in transform board
Use the built-in transforms and expressions, keeping user-defined functions for logic the existing options cannot express
Leave the dates as text in the pipeline and convert them in each Workshop widget, so every app can choose its own format

stem: The logistics tool needs a short list of depot priority codes that exists in no source system; an operations lead keeps it in their head and it rarely changes. What is the simplest way to get it into the pipeline?

choices.text: Ask each dispatcher to type the priority for every shipment by hand in the app, since reference data cannot be added to pipelines
Hard-code each priority as a separate filter in every Workshop module, so the codes never need to exist as data at all
Build a new external database for the codes and set up a Data Connection source and sync just for this one small list
Enter the codes as a manually entered table in the pipeline or upload a small file, since both are documented input methods

stem: A builder starts a new pipeline from a Data Connection source and tries to save it in their personal folder, but saving there is not allowed. What should they do?

choices.text: Save the pipeline in a Project, which is the documented permission boundary for organizing related work, data and access
Ask an administrator to raise the size limit of the personal folder, since pipelines are blocked there only because they are large
Save it in a colleague's personal folder instead, since only the builder's own personal folder blocks new pipelines
Download the pipeline definition to their laptop and keep it there until the workflow is finished and ready for review

stem: A manager questions a late-shipment count in the new app and asks which source tables and which logic produced it. What gives the clearest answer in Foundry?

choices.text: Export the app's table to a spreadsheet and ask the manager to recompute the count from the visible rows by hand
Use Data Lineage to trace the output back through its upstream datasets and the logic that produced each one
Rebuild the entire pipeline from scratch with new names, so that the count can be recalculated and compared with the old one
Ask the builder to recall the steps from memory and write them in an email, since Foundry keeps no record of how outputs were made

stem: An analyst wants a quick look at shipment volumes by region to test an idea this afternoon, while the team also needs a governed, scheduled pipeline feeding objects for the dispatch app. Which pairing of tools fits?

choices.text: Workshop for both needs, since one application should handle ad-hoc analysis and data integration for every team at once
Pipeline Builder for the quick look and Contour for the production pipeline, since Contour is designed for scheduled object outputs
Contour for the quick point-and-click analysis, and Pipeline Builder or Code Repositories for the production pipeline
Data Lineage for the quick look and Data Connection for the production pipeline, since syncs can clean and join data

stem: For the first version of the dispatch tool the team needs a list of late shipments, a filter by warehouse and a reassign button, built quickly and maintained by a small team. Which application builder fits?

choices.text: Workshop, since it builds point-and-click apps on objects and suits low to moderate complexity with lower maintenance cost
Contour, since a dashboard of charts is the standard way for dispatchers to write their decisions back to shipment objects
Data Lineage, since its graph view can be shared with dispatchers and lets them edit shipment rows directly in the graph
Slate, since every first application should use custom HTML, CSS and JavaScript to keep full control over each screen

stem: The first app shows late shipments well, but dispatchers still phone the warehouse to reassign them and nothing records what they decided. What should the next iteration add?

choices.text: Read-only access to the raw carrier dataset, so dispatchers can check source rows before calling the warehouse to reassign
An Action that reassigns the shipment from the app, so the decision is written back to the objects and can be assessed later
A daily export of the late-shipment list to email, so dispatchers can reply with their decisions and someone retypes them weekly
A second dashboard page with more charts of late shipments, since better visibility removes the need to capture any decisions

stem: A sponsor wants the team to integrate every table from all twelve logistics systems before building any application. The team expects that to take months. Which approach matches the platform's guidance on delivering a use case?

choices.text: Integrate all twelve systems first, since any application built on partial data is wasted effort that must be thrown away later
Buy a second platform for the application layer and keep Foundry only for storage, so each tool can be chosen separately later
Build a full set of dashboards for every department before choosing a decision, so users can later say which data they want integrated
Start from the decision to support, work back to the few sources it needs, ship a small working tool and extend it with feedback

stem: A cleaning change merged into the main pipeline this morning has started dropping valid shipments from the output that backs the app. The cause is not yet understood. What is the quickest safe recovery?

choices.text: Delete the pipeline and rebuild it from the raw datasets, since a merged change cannot be undone once it has reached main
Leave the change in place and ask dispatchers to add missing shipments by hand in the app until a fix is ready next month
Turn off every schedule in the project so no outputs change again until the full root cause has been documented in detail
Revert the pipeline to its previous version, rebuild, and investigate the faulty change on a branch before merging a fix

stem: An IT team plans to clean and reshape supplier files with scripts on an external server before loading them into Foundry, so that only tidy data arrives. What does Palantir's guidance on data ingestion favor instead?

choices.text: Keep the external scripts, because data should arrive in Foundry already cleaned so that downstream pipelines remain short and simple
Load only the cleaned columns that applications need today and drop the raw files, so storage and sync time stay as low as possible
Ingest the data as-is from the raw source, then clean it in a versioned Foundry pipeline so every change to the data stays traceable
Ask each supplier to send pre-cleaned files, so that neither the IT team nor Foundry needs to transform the incoming data at all

stem: A data science team already has a demand forecasting model trained in their own notebook environment outside Foundry. They want its predictions to support decisions on Ontology objects. Which statement about models in the platform is accurate?

choices.text: Models must be retrained from scratch inside Foundry, because the platform cannot accept models that were built in an external environment
Externally built models can be imported as libraries, artifacts, containers or APIs, then governed, deployed and used with the Ontology
Only large language models can back logic on objects, so the forecasting model must be replaced by an LLM prompt that predicts demand
Externally built models can only be used by exporting Foundry data to the notebook and copying the predictions back by hand each day

stem: A Workshop application needs a column that shows each shipment's delay risk, calculated from several properties and linked objects at the moment a user opens the app. Which platform capability is designed for this kind of logic?

choices.text: Functions, which run server-side code that can read object properties, traverse links and return values to applications such as Workshop
Data Connection syncs, which pull a pre-calculated risk value from the source system every time a user opens the Workshop application
Markings, which attach calculated values to sensitive objects so that only eligible users can view the computed risk for each shipment
Global Branching, which keeps a separate copy of each shipment so that the risk value can be calculated on a branch before display

stem: An action that approves purchase orders also sends the approval to an external ERP through a webhook. Last week the ERP call failed, yet the order already showed "approved" in Foundry. The team wants Foundry unchanged whenever the ERP call fails. What should they change?

choices.text: Keep the webhook as a side effect but add a second side effect webhook that repeats the same ERP call in case the first one fails
Schedule a nightly data sync from the ERP that overwrites the approval status in Foundry with whatever the ERP recorded that day
Remove the webhook and ask users to type every approval into the ERP by hand after they apply the action in Foundry
Configure the webhook as a writeback, which runs before the action's other rules so that a failed call stops the Ontology changes

stem: When a maintenance ticket is closed through an action, the team wants to notify a chat tool and update two separate reporting systems on a best-effort basis. A slow reporting system must not block the user. Which webhook setup fits?

choices.text: Configure all three calls as side effect webhooks, which run after the object changes and do not hold up the user's success message
Skip webhooks and give each external system read access to the Foundry project so it can poll the ticket objects for changes
Configure the slowest reporting system as the writeback webhook, so the user waits only for that call and the others follow later
Configure all three calls as writeback webhooks, so that the action waits until every external system has confirmed the update

stem: Three teams each built their own app to reassign field technicians, and each app edits the technician data in a slightly different way, with different checks. What does modelling the change as an Ontology action type provide?

choices.text: A dashboard that shows which app changed each technician record, so that managers can correct inconsistent edits by hand afterwards
A nightly reconciliation job that compares the three apps' edits and keeps whichever value was written most recently for each technician
One defined change with shared parameters, rules and validations that every application uses, so edits are applied the same way everywhere
A separate copy of the technician data for each app, so that each team's checks can stay different without affecting the other teams

stem: An analyst must join two very large tables that are not mapped to the Ontology and save the joined result as a new dataset for other Foundry tools. Which point-and-click analysis application fits best?

choices.text: Automate, because it checks conditions on a schedule and can run effects that combine large tables into a new output dataset
Contour, because it analyzes tables at scale, works with data not mapped to the Ontology and can save results as a new dataset
Workshop, because it builds operational applications that read from the object layer and write back changes through actions
Quiver, because it is optimized for object and time series data from the Ontology and for dashboards embedded in Workshop

stem: Reliability engineers want to explore pump sensor readings over time for objects in the Ontology, follow links to each pump's site, embed the resulting dashboard in a Workshop app and record their conclusion through an action. Which application fits?

choices.text: Contour, because it is the platform's tool for large tables and saves its analysis results as new datasets for downstream use
Data Connection, because sensor readings arrive from external systems and must be explored where the sync is configured
Quiver, because it analyzes Ontology object and time series data, follows links natively and can embed dashboards in Workshop
Apollo, because it monitors the health of every environment and sends alerts to engineering teams through existing tools

stem: Warranty claims are triaged from a shared analysis dashboard. Reviewers can filter and chart claims but keep a spreadsheet to record decisions, and the spreadsheets disagree. What is the better fit for this operational triage?

choices.text: Build a Workshop application on the claim objects, with an inbox-style view and actions that write each decision back to the Ontology
Email the dashboard as a PDF every morning so that all reviewers start from the same picture before updating their spreadsheets
Give every reviewer the Editor role on the source dataset so that they can type decisions directly into the raw table rows
Add more charts to the dashboard so that reviewers can see every claim attribute and agree on decisions before writing them down

stem: A team set up Automate to watch for failed pipeline builds and broken data connections, but the setup feels awkward and misses the details they need. According to the Automate docs, what is the better approach?

choices.text: Add more conditions to the same automation until every failure type in the pipeline is covered by a separate notification effect
Use the platform's health checks for monitoring data connections and pipeline builds, and keep Automate for business automation
Move the build logs into the Ontology as objects so that Automate can watch them as ordinary business data conditions
Replace Automate with a Workshop application that operators refresh by hand every hour to look for failed pipeline builds

stem: A company's web team wants to build its own React portal for field staff, hosted outside the standard Foundry applications, reading and writing Ontology objects with type-safe code. Which platform component is designed for this?

choices.text: Global Branching, because it gives the portal its own branch of the Ontology where external code is allowed to make changes
Data Connection, because it moves data to external systems on a schedule so the portal can read a nightly copy of the objects
Contour, because its expression language lets developers query tables and return results to any external web application
The Ontology SDK (OSDK), which generates typed code from the Ontology for TypeScript, Python and Java so apps can read and write it

stem: A security reviewer worries that a new OSDK-based app will let any logged-in user see every object in the Ontology, because the app holds an application token. Which description of OSDK security is accurate?

choices.text: OSDK apps bypass Foundry permissions by design, so sensitive objects must be copied into a separate Ontology before going live
The OSDK token is scoped to the Ontology entities the app needs, and reads still respect the signed-in user's own permissions
The application token grants full access to the whole Ontology, so the app must filter out restricted objects in its own code
OSDK apps can only read public datasets, so the reviewer's concern applies only to objects that have no markings applied

stem: A logistics company wants an AI-powered function to reroute delayed shipments. Leaders want value quickly but fear wrong reroutes, which are costly. Which first step matches the progressive path from augmentation to automation?

choices.text: Have the function propose reroutes that planners review through actions, capture their feedback, and automate more as trust grows
Keep rerouting fully manual and use the function only for a monthly report, so that AI never influences an operational decision
Delay the project until the function has been tested on every possible shipment scenario, so that it never needs human review at all
Let the function apply every reroute automatically from day one, since review steps slow down the business and reduce the value of AI

stem: A manager asks what Palantir AIP adds on top of Foundry. Which description matches the AIP documentation?

choices.text: AIP is the deployment service that installs Foundry upgrades across cloud and air-gapped environments using release channels
AIP is a single chatbot model trained by Palantir on each customer's data, replacing the need for Ontology objects and actions
AIP connects AI with an organization's data and operations, with builder tools such as AIP Logic, Chatbot Studio and Evals on the Ontology
AIP is a separate data warehouse that copies Foundry data into a new store so that language models can read it without Foundry's controls

stem: A CIO worries that building AI workflows on AIP would tie the company to one model vendor and to a single model for every task. Which statement matches the AIP documentation?

choices.text: The model is chosen once for the whole enrollment at setup time, and changing it later means rebuilding every AIP workflow from scratch
AIP runs only a language model built by Palantir, so every workflow uses that same model whatever its task, cost or quality needs are
Each model provider needs its own copy of the Ontology data outside Foundry, so adding a provider becomes a new integration project
AIP supports models from several providers, so builders can pick the model best suited to each use case, subject to enrollment availability

stem: A team wants to switch an LLM-backed function to a newer model because a colleague says it is "better". The function classifies insurance claims in production. What should they do before switching?

choices.text: Run an evaluation suite with representative test cases on both models, compare the metrics and check variance across several runs
Keep the old model and lengthen the prompt with more instructions, because prompt length matters more than model choice
Switch immediately and watch user complaints for a week, because LLM behavior cannot be measured in any way before real use
Ask a few users to try three claims each on the new model and switch if most of them say the answers look reasonable

stem: A user holds the Owner role on a project, yet cannot open one dataset inside it that carries a PII marking. Another Owner of the same project can open it. What explains this?

choices.text: Markings only apply to Viewers, so the dataset must have a file-level role grant that removes the user's Owner rights
The dataset is still building, and Owners cannot open datasets until every downstream transform has finished running
The Owner role expires after a period of inactivity, so the user must ask an administrator to grant the Owner role again
Markings are a mandatory control, so the user must be a member of every marking on the dataset regardless of their project role

stem: An analyst builds a summary dataset from a source dataset marked PII and shares the new dataset's project with a colleague who is not eligible for PII. The colleague can see the dataset in the project but cannot read its data. Why?

choices.text: The colleague needs the Owner role on the summary dataset, since Viewers can see dataset names but not the rows inside them
Markings propagate to data derived from a marked dataset, so the summary inherits the PII marking unless it is explicitly removed
Sharing a project never includes datasets created in the last 24 hours, so the colleague must wait until the next day
Summary datasets are always private to their creator until the creator copies the data into a new dataset with a new name

stem: An administrator plans to make the PII marking the main way to give people access: once someone completes PII training, they would get every PII dataset in the platform. What does the markings guidance say?

choices.text: That design is recommended, because markings are the simplest way to give eligible users access to all data they might ever need
Markings should replace project roles entirely, since roles are discretionary and therefore less secure than mandatory markings
Markings restrict access and define eligibility; actual access should still come from role grants on the projects a user needs
Markings should only be applied after data has been shared, so that they never block users who already had access to the data

stem: A new team lead will onboard twenty analysts to a project. What is the recommended way to manage their access?

choices.text: Grant a group a role at the project level, so that project contents inherit the role and access is managed in one place
Create a separate personal copy of the project for each analyst so that their work never touches shared resources
Share links to the project's datasets so that each analyst receives a direct role grant on the resources they open
Grant each analyst a role on every individual file and folder they need, so that access matches each file exactly

stem: An investigations unit must ensure that people outside a case cannot even discover that the case's project exists in search results. Which control fits this requirement?

choices.text: A Workshop application in front of the project data, so that users see only the cases that the app's filters choose to show them
A Discoverer role for everyone outside the case, since Discoverers can find the project but cannot read any of its data
A marking for the case, since users who lack the marking do not see marked resources in search or in the project and folder view
A naming convention that gives the project a neutral name, so that outsiders who find it in search cannot tell what it contains

stem: A team wants to change the logic and schema of a Pipeline Builder output that backs an object type, adjust the object type to match, and test the full workflow before anything reaches production users. Which capability supports this?

choices.text: A copy of the whole project, in which the team rebuilds the pipeline and object type and then deletes the original resources
Global Branching, which lets them change several resources on one branch, test end-to-end, get approvals and then merge into main
Markings, which hide the changed object type from production users until the team removes the marking after testing ends
Apollo release channels, which push each pipeline change automatically to a canary environment before it reaches production

stem: A platform lead asks whether Global Branching makes release management across development, test and production environments unnecessary. Which answer matches the documentation?

choices.text: Yes, because merging a branch into main automatically deploys the same change to every environment the organization operates
Yes, because release management only exists for code repositories and is not used for pipelines or Ontology resources
No, because Global Branching is limited to datasets, so release management is still needed for every Ontology change
No, they are complementary: branching isolates development work, release management moves versions across environments

stem: A tester applied several actions while testing on a global branch and is worried because production users cannot see the edits the actions made. What explains this?

choices.text: The actions failed silently, because actions are disabled on every branch and only run after the branch is merged into main
The edits were stored in a cache that refreshes every night, so production users will see the tester's edits the next morning
Production users lack a marking for branch data, so they must request it before they can see the edits made during testing
This is expected: actions can run on a branch without writing edits back to main, so testing does not change production data

stem: In the platform architecture, which role does Palantir Apollo play?

choices.text: It is the Ontology's write engine that commits action edits and streams changes to operational systems in real time
It is the AI layer that gives builders access to language models from several providers through AIP Logic and agents
It manages and deploys software across many environments, including air-gapped ones, with constraints and release channels
It is the governance layer that decides which users may read each dataset through markings and project roles

stem: A new builder is following a guide to bring data from a company S3 bucket into Foundry. The guide asks them to create a source first and a sync afterwards. What is the difference between the two?

choices.text: The source is the dataset in Foundry that stores the imported files, while a sync is the network rule that lets Foundry reach the external bucket on a defined port and protocol
The source holds the connection to the external system, such as its location, credentials and network path, while a sync defines which data to read and which dataset receives it
The source is a scheduled job that copies data from the bucket every night, while a sync is the encrypted credential record that the job uses to sign in to the external system
The source lists the users who may read the imported data, while a sync is the transform that cleans and joins the raw files before they are stored in the output dataset

stem: A team on a cloud-hosted Foundry enrollment wants to connect to an S3 bucket that is reachable over the public Internet. Which kind of network egress policy fits this source?

choices.text: A direct connection policy, because the bucket is reachable from Foundry's network, which for a cloud-hosted Foundry instance means the public Internet
A private link policy, because the docs require private links for every cloud storage service so that no traffic between Foundry and AWS crosses the Internet
No egress policy at all, because storage buckets are reached through the cloud provider's backbone and Foundry never applies firewall rules to that traffic
An agent proxy policy, because every connection from Foundry to a storage bucket has to pass through an agent installed inside the customer's own network

stem: A company runs a cloud-hosted Foundry enrollment and wants to sync tables from a PostgreSQL database in its own data center. The database is not reachable from the Internet. Which setup fits the recommended architecture?

choices.text: Open an inbound firewall rule from Foundry's egress IP ranges to the database and attach a direct connection policy, since direct is the only option for databases
Export the tables to CSV files every night with a script, upload them by hand into a Foundry dataset, and skip the source because databases cannot be connected
Install a Data Connection agent inside the company network and use a Foundry worker source with an agent proxy egress policy, so compute runs in Foundry
Install a Data Connection agent and configure it as an agent worker that runs every sync on the agent host, since this is the recommended mode for new sources

stem: A manager asks why a builder had to request an egress policy before a new source could connect, even though the external system is a well-known public service. What is the purpose of an egress policy?

choices.text: It sets how often a sync may run against the external system, so that scheduled jobs do not overload the source with requests during business hours
It allowlists a specific destination and path that workloads may reach, since Foundry blocks outbound traffic unless a policy explicitly permits it
It records which Foundry users have read the imported data, so that auditors can trace every dataset back to the person who first opened it in Foundry
It encrypts the credentials of the source, so that passwords and tokens stored in Foundry cannot be read by users who only have viewer access to the project

stem: A builder proposed a direct connection egress policy for a partner API yesterday, attached it to a new source today, and the source still cannot connect. The policy's state shows Pending approval. What explains this, and what is the next step?

choices.text: Workloads using a policy that is still pending approval fail to run, so an administrator with the egress management workflow must approve it first
A pending policy only allows read traffic, so the builder should switch the source to write mode until the policy finishes its review cycle
The policy needs a day to replicate to every Foundry region, so the builder should wait and retry the connection without contacting anyone else
The source must be recreated whenever a policy changes state, so the builder should delete the source and build a new one with the same settings

stem: An Information Security Officer approved an egress policy for an internal API and shared it with a builder as a Viewer. The builder can see the policy but cannot attach it to a new source. What is missing?

choices.text: The builder needs the Information Security Officer role too, because only that role may attach any approved egress policy to a source
The builder needs the Owner role on the Foundry project, because egress policies can only be attached to sources that live in a project the user owns
The builder needs to wait for the next platform release, because newly approved policies can only be attached after the following upgrade
The builder needs Import permission on that policy, because viewers can see a policy exists but only importers may attach it to a workload

stem: A builder sets up a PostgreSQL source on a Foundry worker. The egress policy is active and correct, but the connection test fails with a PKIX path building error. The database uses a certificate issued by the company's internal certificate authority. What should the builder do?

choices.text: Switch the source to a legacy agent worker, since Foundry worker sources cannot connect to any database that uses a non-public certificate authority
Replace the database password with a personal user account, since PKIX errors appear when a service account lacks the privileges to read the tables
Add the internal certificate authority's certificate to the source as a server certificate, so Foundry can trust the certificate the database presents
Request a second egress policy for the same host on a different port, since PKIX errors mean the network route is too narrow for an encrypted session

stem: A database team says their server requires mutual TLS: every client must prove its own identity with a certificate before any query is accepted. What does the Foundry source need in that case?

choices.text: A personal user token in place of the service account password, because mutual TLS checks the identity of the human who triggers each sync run
A second egress policy of the agent proxy type, because mutual TLS connections can only travel through an agent installed inside the database team's network
A server certificate only, provided as the certificate without a private key, because server certificates are how Foundry proves its own identity to the database
A client certificate with its private key, because in mutual TLS the Foundry client presents its own certificate so the database can verify Foundry

stem: A builder creates a batch sync from a new source and must choose an output location for the synced dataset. Which choice follows the documented best practice?

choices.text: Save the dataset in the same project as the source, so all data from that connector is permissioned uniformly through the project's roles
Save the dataset in each analyst's personal folder, so that every person who needs the data owns a private copy that nobody else can change
Save the dataset into an existing curated dataset, so the new rows are added to the data that applications already use without new links
Save the dataset in the project of the first downstream application, so the application team controls who may read the raw synced data

stem: Several developers ask for Editor access on a production database source so they can add syncs whenever they like. The source credentials can also write to and delete from the database. What should the platform owner weigh first?

choices.text: Editors of a source can only create new syncs and never run queries, so granting Edit widely is safe as long as the output datasets are marked
Editors of a source can change the external system if the credentials allow it, so Edit should go only to people trusted with that account's full access
Editors of a source automatically receive a copy of every synced dataset, so the main concern is storage cost rather than the risk to the database
Editors of a source are limited by the egress policy to read-only traffic, so write access in the credentials can never be used through Foundry

stem: A finance analyst needs to build a report on invoice data that a nightly sync brings into Foundry. The analyst has no need to configure connections. How should access be given?

choices.text: Send the analyst the source credentials, so that the analyst can query the external database directly from a personal tool for the report
Make the analyst an Editor of the source, so that the analyst can open the connection, explore the tables and copy any rows the report needs
Add the analyst as an importer on the egress policy, so that the analyst can reach the external database from any Foundry workload
Grant access to the synced dataset, for example by importing it into the analyst's project, without sharing the source or its credentials

stem: A source connects to an HR database that contains personal data. The team plans to add a marking to each synced dataset after it lands. What does the Data Connection guidance recommend instead?

choices.text: Mark the source with every marking that applies to its data, since markings on the source propagate to the datasets its syncs produce
Leave both the source and the datasets unmarked, and rely on the egress policy to stop personal data from being shown to analysts who open the datasets
Mark only the downstream Workshop application, since markings on sources and datasets are ignored once the data is shown inside an application
Mark only the external database itself, since Foundry copies the database's own permission settings onto every dataset that a sync produces

stem: A nightly batch sync failed halfway through copying files because of a network interruption. Users ask whether the output dataset now holds a mix of old and new files. What is the state of the dataset?

choices.text: It is locked until an administrator repairs it by hand, because a failed run leaves the dataset in a broken state
It is empty, because a failed run clears the output dataset so that no outdated data can be used downstream
It is unchanged from its state before the run, because the sync writes in one transaction that is aborted on failure
It holds every file copied before the failure, because each file is committed on its own as soon as it reaches Foundry

stem: A team connects two systems in the same week: an S3 bucket full of CSV and PDF files, and a PostgreSQL database with an orders table. Which kind of batch sync fits each one?

choices.text: A table batch sync for the bucket, which infers one schema for all files, and a file batch sync for the database, which exports each table as a file
A file batch sync for the bucket, which copies files without a schema, and a table batch sync for the database, which reads rows through a query
A streaming sync for the bucket, because files arrive continuously, and a media sync for the database, because each row is stored as a media item
A file batch sync for both systems, because every batch sync stores raw files and the database rows are converted into CSV files afterwards

stem: A warehouse list of about 2,000 rows is maintained in a database, and rows are often edited or removed. A builder wants the Foundry dataset to always match the current list after each nightly sync. Which transaction type should the sync use?

choices.text: APPEND, because each run adds the new rows and also removes the rows that were deleted in the database
APPEND, because it is always faster and never needs to read the rows that already exist in the dataset
SNAPSHOT, because each run replaces the previously ingested data with the current contents of the table
SNAPSHOT, because it keeps every earlier version of each row visible side by side in the current view

stem: A builder has configured a table batch sync with a query but has not run it yet. They want to confirm the query returns the expected columns before scheduling it. What does Data Connection offer for this?

choices.text: A preview of the sync output, which shows a sample of the selected table results, limited to the first rows, before the sync is ever run
A test schedule that runs the sync every five minutes for a day, so that the builder can watch the output dataset grow before going live
A dry-run build that writes the full result into a temporary dataset and deletes it after one hour, so that every row can be compared with the source
A schema report that the source owner must request from Palantir Support, which lists the expected columns of every table that the sync reads

stem: A new PostgreSQL source on a Foundry worker fails its connection test with a timeout before any login attempt. The attached egress policy allows the database host on port 443, while the database listens on port 5432. What is the most likely fix?

choices.text: Increase the sync's maximum duration setting, since the connection test stops early when the sync is allowed only a short time to run
Add a server certificate for the database, since a timeout before login always means Foundry does not trust the certificate that the database presents
Reset the database password and enter it again, since a stale password is the usual reason a connection times out before the login step starts
Request a policy that allows the database host on port 5432, since the attached policy does not match the port the source connects to

stem: A builder can explore a database source and preview its tables without any problem, but one specific batch sync on that source keeps failing. Where should the builder look first?

choices.text: At the agent host's operating system, because every failing sync on a Foundry worker source is executed on the customer's own agent machine
At the configuration of that sync, such as its query, filters or schema settings, since the source connection itself is evidently working
At the downstream transforms, because a failing sync is usually caused by a pipeline that reads its output dataset during the sync run
At the egress policy of the source, because a working exploration session does not prove that Foundry can reach the external database at all

stem: An approved egress policy for a supplier API turns out to name the wrong host: the supplier moved the API to a new domain. A builder wants to change the policy's destination to the new domain and keep using it. What should happen instead?

choices.text: Keep the old policy and add the new domain as an alias in the source settings, since sources may reach any host that resolves through an approved domain
Edit the destination on the existing policy as its importer, since importers may update the address of any active policy they already use in a source
Propose a new policy for the new domain and have it approved, since a policy's destination cannot be changed after creation; the old one can be revoked
Delete the old policy and recreate it with the same name and the new domain, since deleting a policy is how its destination gets corrected in Foundry

stem: A batch sync started running twice every night, a few minutes apart. The builder set a schedule on the sync in Data Connection, and a colleague later scheduled the same sync together with others in Data Lineage. What should they change?

choices.text: Switch the sync to APPEND, because a snapshot sync is always run twice by the build system to confirm that both outputs match
Keep a single schedule, because the docs say a sync should not be scheduled from both Data Connection and Data Lineage at once
Delete the sync and create it again, because a sync that has been scheduled in Data Lineage can never be scheduled in Data Connection
Keep both schedules and add a build policy, because two schedules on one sync are the documented way to retry a run that may fail

stem: An administrator finds an old source configured as an agent worker that runs its syncs on a server in the data center. A new source must reach the same on-premises network. What does the current guidance recommend for the new source?

choices.text: Create it on a Foundry worker with an agent proxy policy, since agent worker is legacy and agents now act only as network proxies for new sources
Configure it as another agent worker on the same host, since the docs recommend that all sources reaching an on-premises network share one agent worker
Copy the old source's credentials into the new source's agent host file, since agent proxy sources store their secrets on the agent machine's disk
Create it as a direct connection without any agent, since Foundry worker sources reach on-premises networks on their own once the source is saved

stem: A builder with Editor rights on a project tries to create a new source in it, but is not allowed to. Colleagues in another organization on the same enrollment can create sources without any extra role. What is the most likely reason?

choices.text: The builder's egress policy was revoked, and a revoked policy blocks its importers from creating any new source anywhere on the enrollment
The project has reached its maximum number of sources, so the builder must delete an unused source before any new one can be saved there
Source creation is limited to Information Security Officers on every enrollment, so the colleagues must already hold that role without knowing it
The builder's organization has role-based source creation enabled, so creating a source needs an organization role with the source creation workflow

stem: A builder is about to create a source for the company's sales database and plans to enter their own database login, since it already has access to every table. What does the documentation recommend instead?

choices.text: Use no credentials and rely on the egress policy, since an approved egress policy authenticates Foundry to the database on the builder's behalf
Use a dedicated service account with credentials scoped to the access Foundry needs, provisioned according to the organization's own guidelines
Use the database administrator's account, so that the source never runs into permission errors when new tables are added to the database later
Use the personal login for now and replace it later, since sources cannot change credentials once a sync has been created and run on them

stem: An S3 source with the right egress policy and IAM credentials can list the files in the bucket during exploration, but every batch sync fails with an access denied error when reading the files. What should the AWS administrator check?

choices.text: Whether a second egress policy exists for the bucket, since listing and reading files are sent over two different network paths from Foundry
Whether the sync uses SNAPSHOT, since an S3 sync with APPEND can only list files and must be switched before any content can be read
Whether the bucket uses an internal certificate authority, since reading file contents needs a server certificate that listing files does not
Whether the IAM user is allowed to read objects in the bucket, since listing files and reading their contents need different AWS permissions

stem: A network team must prepare their firewall before a Data Connection agent is installed to reach an internal database through an agent proxy policy. Which connections does this setup need?

choices.text: An inbound rule from Foundry's egress IP ranges to the agent host, since Foundry connects to the agent to collect the data it has read
An outbound path from the database to Foundry, since the database pushes every changed row to the platform as soon as it is committed
An outbound path from the agent host to Foundry and a path from the agent host to the database, with no inbound path from Foundry
An inbound rule from Foundry's egress IP ranges to the database, since Foundry opens a direct session to the database through the firewall

stem: A planning team describes one of its weekly decisions: "We look at stock levels per warehouse, run our demand forecast model, and then reorder from a supplier." In Palantir's breakdown of a decision into data, logic and actions, where does the demand forecast model belong?

choices.text: Logic, because a forecast is reasoning that evaluates the decision and enriches its context, alongside business rules and optimization models
Data, because the forecast produces numbers that describe the world, so it counts as one more fact about stock levels next to the warehouse records
None of the three, because models are managed in a separate data science workbench and stay outside the decision model of the platform itself
Actions, because the forecast directly triggers the supplier reorder, so it is part of how the decision takes effect in the operational systems

stem: A logistics company already has dashboards that show late shipments every morning. A manager asks what would make a new solution "operational" rather than "analytical" in the sense Palantir uses. Which answer matches that distinction?

choices.text: The operational solution refreshes its data in real time, while an analytical one refreshes on a schedule; the speed of the data is the defining difference
The operational solution is used by frontline staff, while an analytical one is used by managers; the audience of the screens is the defining difference
The operational solution replaces the existing dashboards entirely, while an analytical one runs next to them as a second reporting tool for managers
The operational solution lets users and agents act on what they see, and those decisions are written back to the Ontology or source systems

stem: An enterprise architect maps three needs onto Palantir's architecture: syncing data from an ERP, training a machine learning model, and running an event-driven automation when a record changes. Which grouping of services matches the Architecture Center's description?

choices.text: Logic Services for the ERP sync, Data Services for training the model, and Workflow Services for the event-driven automation
Data Services for the ERP sync, Logic Services for training the model, and Workflow Services for the event-driven automation
Data Services for the ERP sync and for training the model, and Logic Services for the event-driven automation that reacts to changes
Workflow Services for the ERP sync, Logic Services for training the model, and Data Services for the event-driven automation

stem: A CIO asks why the company should model its operations in the Palantir Ontology when it already has a well-run data warehouse with clean, joined tables. Which answer reflects how Palantir's documentation explains the Ontology's value?

choices.text: The Ontology captures decisions, not only data: the logic and actions around them, so people and agents can act on operations, not just report
The Ontology replaces the warehouse's SQL with a visual query tool, so analysts no longer need to write joins when they build their weekly reports
The Ontology stores data more cheaply than a warehouse, so moving the tables into it lowers storage costs while keeping the same reports running
The Ontology guarantees better data quality than a warehouse, because objects cannot hold missing or inconsistent values once they are created

stem: Palantir's "Why create an Ontology?" page models each operational decision with four components. Three are data, logic and action. Which is the fourth, and what does it ensure?

choices.text: Lineage, which ensures that every dataset used in the decision can be traced back to the source system that first produced it
Scale, which ensures that the same decision can be repeated across thousands of users and agents without slowing down the platform
Security, which ensures that the decision complies with operational policies for both the people and the agents involved in it
Feedback, which ensures that the outcome of each decision is collected and used later to retrain the models behind the logic

stem: A maintenance team wants its AI workflows to work with three kinds of information beyond plain tables: thousands of repair manuals, photos of damaged parts, and part numbers that must follow a strict format. How does Palantir's platform overview describe the Ontology's support for this?

choices.text: The Ontology requires every manual and photo to be converted into rows of text before loading, and the format rules are written into each application separately
The Ontology handles only structured tables, so manuals and photos must stay in a separate document system that AI workflows query on their own, outside the model
The Ontology supports extended primitives such as semantic search for unstructured text, media references for images, and value types that add constraints to data
The Ontology stores manuals and photos as long text properties on each part object, and format checks are left to the language model that reads those properties

stem: A supply chain analyst wants to substitute a raw material in one product line, but the same material feeds other products and the knock-on effects are unclear. Planners want to see the consequences before anything changes in production. Which approach matches the platform overview's guidance for this kind of what-if question?

choices.text: Export the affected tables to a spreadsheet, edit the material there, and estimate the downstream effects by hand before entering the change in production
Describe the substitution to an AI agent in a long prompt, and accept its written summary of the likely effects as the basis for the production decision
Apply the substitution in the live Ontology during a quiet hour, watch the forecasts react, and roll it back afterwards if the results look worse than expected
Stage the substitution on a branch of the Ontology, and run forecasts and other analyses on top of that potential change before anyone commits it to production

stem: An AI agent drafts freight quotes for customers. Its explanations read well, but the totals are sometimes wrong because it does the rate arithmetic itself. The company already has a tested pricing calculation used by its quoting system. What fixes the root cause?

choices.text: Add worked examples of quote calculations to the agent's prompt, so that it copies the method and repeats it correctly for every new customer request
Connect the existing pricing calculation to the Ontology as logic and offer it to the agent as a tool, so totals come from the tested calculation
Switch the agent to a larger language model, because a stronger model makes fewer arithmetic mistakes and needs no change to the logic it can reach
Keep the agent as it is and ask sales staff to recalculate every total by hand before sending it, so wrong quotes are caught before customers see them

stem: The Architecture Center says the Ontology is not a thin semantic layer but a system made of a Language, an Engine and a Toolchain. Which part provides the read and write architecture, such as high-scale queries, subscriptions to changes and transactional updates?

choices.text: The Engine, because it substantiates every component of the Language and is where queries and updates against the Ontology are executed
The Workflow Services, because they run interactive compute, so they hold the read and write architecture of the Ontology system as well
The Toolchain, because developers use it to build applications, so it is the part that stores data and runs every transactional update
The Language, because it defines the objects, links and actions, so it also executes every query and every write made against them

stem: A retailer's business intelligence team uses an external BI tool every day and is worried that adopting Palantir means abandoning it. How does Palantir's documentation describe the relationship between the platform's analytics and existing BI tools?

choices.text: The platform interoperates with common BI tools through dedicated connectors, and its own analytics can also write results back to the Ontology
The platform requires BI tools to connect through the Ontology SDK only, so each dashboard has to be rewritten as a custom code application
The platform supports only its own analysis tools, so reports must be rebuilt in them before the existing BI tool can be switched off for good

stem: A data governance lead says the Ontology sounds like the data catalog the company already has, which lists every table with a description and an owner. Which comparison matches Palantir's Ontology documentation?

choices.text: A catalog stores the data itself while the Ontology stores only descriptions, so the Ontology must always read through the catalog before an application shows an object
A catalog describes datasets; the Ontology maps them into objects, properties and links with metadata, and adds action types and functions to change them under governance

stem: A pilot chatbot answers questions about a company's supply chain from a folder of PDF reports. Users complain that it gives generic advice and cannot tell which open orders a late supplier affects, or do anything about them. What change addresses the root cause?

choices.text: Move to a larger language model, because a stronger model will infer the affected orders from the reports without any change to its data access
Add more PDF reports to the folder, because a larger document collection gives the model enough examples to identify affected orders by itself
Give the chatbot a longer system prompt describing the supply chain, so that it understands the business well enough to recommend actions
Connect the chatbot to the Ontology, so it can use supplier and order objects, their links and permitted actions as tools in its answers

stem: A new analyst who knows spreadsheets asks how Ontology concepts compare with a dataset. Which comparison matches Palantir's own description?

choices.text: An object type is like a column, an object is like a dataset, a property is like a row, and a link type is like a filter applied to one dataset
An object type is like a row, an object is like a field value, a property is like a dataset, and a link type is like a sort order on two columns
An object type is like a dataset, an object is like a row, a property is like a column, and a link type is like a join between two datasets
An object type is like a join, an object is like a column, a property is like a filtered set of rows, and a link type is like a single field value

stem: In a fleet Ontology, `Aircraft` is defined with properties such as tail number and model. A dispatcher builds a view showing "all aircraft currently grounded for maintenance". What is that collection called in Ontology terms?

choices.text: An action type, because a grounded aircraft is the result of a change in status and the action defines which aircraft belong together
An object set, a collection of object instances that represents a group of real-world entities, such as a filtered set of aircraft
A new object type, because every filtered group of aircraft needs its own schema definition before it can be shown in an application
A link type, because the grounded aircraft are related to a maintenance status and that relationship defines the collection of aircraft

stem: An operations lead can open a `Plant` object and an `Order` object separately in the Ontology, but cannot move from a plant with a raw-material shortage to the customer orders it is due to fulfill. Both object types are backed by up-to-date data. What is most likely missing?

choices.text: An action type on `Plant` that creates new orders, because orders become reachable from a plant only once they were created by that plant

A link type between `Plant` and `Order`, which defines the relationship so applications and agents can navigate from a plant to its orders
A property on the `Order` object type that stores the plant's full address as text, so that users can copy it into a search to find related plants

stem: An HR Ontology has an `Employee` object type. An app must show each employee's direct manager and each manager's team, and every manager is also an employee. A builder proposes a separate `Manager` object type holding a copy of the managers' data. What does the Ontology offer instead?

choices.text: A shared property called manager on every object type, so each employee holds the manager's full record as a value and the team is built from it
An action type that copies a manager's record into each team member's object, so the app reads the manager details without following a link
An interface called `Manager` that each employee object implements, so managers become a separate group of objects with their own copied data

stem: Palantir's documentation divides Ontology elements into "semantic" and "kinetic" ones. Which grouping is correct?

choices.text: Semantic: objects, properties and links; kinetic: actions, functions and dynamic security, which enable change under governance
Semantic: datasets and virtual tables; kinetic: objects and links, because objects are the part of the platform that users can edit
Semantic: object types and action types; kinetic: link types and functions, because links carry changes from one object to another
Semantic: action types and functions; kinetic: objects, properties and links, because the data is what moves through the platform

stem: A stakeholder asks what the Palantir Ontology actually sits on and what it connects. Which description matches the Ontology overview in the documentation?

choices.text: It sits on top of the user interface only, as a set of labels for screens, and does not connect to any datasets, virtual tables or models
It sits on top of the language models only, as a prompt library, and connects them to chat interfaces without any link to company data

stem: A transport company models `Truck`, `Ship` and `Aircraft` as separate object types, each with its own extra properties. A dashboard must list all of them by name and current location, and work with any vehicle type added later without changes. Which Ontology feature fits?

choices.text: An interface describing the shared shape (name and location) that each vehicle object type implements, so workflows treat them consistently
An action type that copies every vehicle into a fourth combined object type, so the dashboard reads one merged type with all the shared fields
An object set per vehicle type joined in the dashboard, so the dashboard combines three separate lists and adds one more list for each new type
A link type connecting `Truck`, `Ship` and `Aircraft` to each other, so the dashboard can start from one type and follow links to reach the others

stem: Several object types in a hospital Ontology (`Patient`, `Staff Member`, `Visitor`) each have a "date of birth" field. The data team wants one consistent definition and central metadata for it instead of three separately managed copies. What does the Ontology provide for this?

choices.text: An object set containing all three object types, so the date of birth is defined once for the set instead of once on every object type
An action type that edits the date of birth on all three object types at once, so the values and their metadata always stay identical
A shared property, which can be used on multiple object types and keeps the property's modeling and metadata consistent and centrally managed

stem: A customer success manager wants a single page for each customer that gathers key information, linked objects such as open tickets and contracts, related metrics and the dashboards relevant to that customer. Which Ontology-aware capability is designed for this?

choices.text: A shared property on the customer, which collects the tickets, contracts and metrics in one field so that they can be shown on a single page
Object Views, which serve as a central hub for all information and workflows related to a particular object, including its linked objects
A link type from each customer to a dashboard, which turns the dashboard into the customer's page and shows the linked objects inside it
An object set saved per customer, which stores a copy of each customer's tickets and contracts so the manager can open them from one list

stem: Sales and finance each built their own tables called "customer", with different rules for what counts as an active customer. An AI agent and two applications now give conflicting counts depending on which table they read. What does Palantir's approach recommend?

choices.text: Give the AI agent access to both tables and let it choose the right definition each time, because a capable model can infer which rule fits the question
Keep both tables and add a note to each application that explains the difference, so users know which count to trust for their own purpose
Build a third table that averages the two counts, so that every consumer receives a single number that sits between the two competing rules
Model one `Customer` object type in the Ontology with agreed properties and metadata, so the agent and both applications read the same definition

stem: A new builder created a separate object type for each of the company's 40 warehouses (`Warehouse Berlin`, `Warehouse Lyon` and so on). Applications now need 40 versions of every filter, and adding a warehouse requires a new type. What is the conceptual mistake?

choices.text: The warehouses should have been modeled as properties of a single company object, one property per warehouse holding its details as text

The warehouses should be one `Warehouse` object type, where each warehouse is an object, so new warehouses are just new objects or rows

stem: A company plans to give AI agents access to its Ontology. The security team asks how the agents' access to sensitive objects and actions will be controlled. Which statement matches Palantir's documentation?

choices.text: Agents are controlled only by instructions in their prompts, which tell them which objects to avoid and which actions they must not run

stem: A new builder confuses two kinetic elements of the Ontology, action types and functions. Which statement correctly contrasts them as the Ontology core concepts page defines them?

choices.text: An action type defines a set of edits a user can make to objects, with side effects; a function is code-based logic that takes inputs and returns an output
