An action type is code that takes inputs and returns an output; a function is the form that end users fill in when they change an object's properties

stem: A team needs nightly data from a vendor's REST API in a Foundry dataset. They created a REST API source in Data Connection, but cannot find a way to add a batch sync to it. What does the documentation recommend?

choices.text: Import the source into a Python transforms repository and write an external transform that calls the API and writes the output dataset
Ask the vendor for a nightly CSV export instead, because Foundry can bring REST API data in only when it arrives as uploaded files
Move the source to an agent worker, because batch syncs from REST API sources are only offered when the connection runs on an agent
Add a webhook to an action behind a Workshop button, and have a user press it each night so the API response is saved as dataset rows

stem: A builder created a REST API source with an active egress policy. In the Python transforms repository, the source does not show up when they search for it to import. Which missing step is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The egress policy must be created a second time inside the repository settings before the source can appear in the import search list
The source has not completed a successful batch sync yet, and only sources with at least one finished sync can be imported into code
The source has not been set to allow imports into code repositories, which is a setting in the source's code import configuration
The repository is a Python repository, while sources can only be imported into TypeScript functions repositories that call external APIs

stem: A source is set to allow imports into code. A developer holds the Viewer role on the source and Editor on the repository, yet the import into the repository is refused. What should the developer request?

choices.text: Nothing about roles: Viewer is enough, so the refusal must come from the API rejecting the developer's personal login credentials
Owner on the repository, because only repository owners may add new external systems, even when they cannot see the source itself
An Information Security Officer must first enable external systems in the repository settings before any source can be imported
At least Editor access on the source itself, which the documentation names as the minimum role needed to import it into a repository

stem: An older transform calls a partner API with an API key written into the repository code. Security asks that the key can be rotated without code changes and that two other repositories reuse the same connection. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Store the key in a small Foundry dataset that each transform reads at run time, so rotation means updating one row instead of editing code
Move to a source-based external transform: keep the key as a secret on a Data Connection source and import that source into each repository
Keep the key in the code but move it to a protected branch, so only reviewers can read it and rotation happens through a reviewed pull request
Copy the key into each of the three repositories so each team controls its own value and a rotation in one repository cannot break the others

stem: An external transform reads a Foundry dataset of product codes and calls a pricing API once per code. The check fails because Foundry inputs are not allowed with this source, although no data is meant to leave Foundry. What fixes it?

choices.text: Copy the product codes into the code as a fixed list, because external transforms are never allowed to read Foundry datasets as their inputs
Remove every marking from the product code dataset first, because external transforms may only read Foundry inputs that carry no markings at all
Switch the transform to a larger compute profile, because this error appears when the input dataset is too large to send along with the request
The source owner enables exports to this source and selects which markings and organizations may be exported, as the docs require for any Foundry input

stem: A builder sets up a REST API source for use in an external transform and chooses an agent worker during setup. The transform cannot use the connection. What does the external transforms guide say about the worker choice?

choices.text: Agent workers are required for any API that needs authentication, so the problem must instead be a missing secret on the source
The source must use a Foundry worker, because the guide states that agent worker connections are not supported for external transforms
The worker choice does not matter for code, because repositories always open their own connection that ignores the source settings
Both workers work, but an agent worker needs a second egress policy added to the repository before the transform can use the source

stem: A builder finishes the transform that calls a REST API, commits it with a short message, and sees the code checks pass. An hour later, the output dataset still does not exist in the project. What explains this?

choices.text: The checks only pass after the dataset exists, so a pass means the dataset was written to a different project than the one opened
Commits made in a branch are discarded after an hour unless a reviewer approves them, so the build never had any code to run on
Committing labels the change and runs checks; the output dataset is created or updated only when a build of the transform is run
The output appears only after a Workshop application references it, because unused datasets are not written to the project folder

stem: An external transform feeds a dataset that an app uses every day. A developer wants to change how the API response is parsed and check the result on real data first. Which workflow fits the Code Repositories guidance?

choices.text: Make the change in a personal branch, build it there to get a branch version of the dataset, then open a pull request for review and merge
Edit the code directly on the master branch and build at night, because a nightly build gives users the fewest hours with any changed data
Change the code on master and build at once, then revert the commit right away if users report problems with the data in their app
Copy the repository into a new project, change the copy and build there, then delete the original repository once the new output looks right

stem: A new external transform calls a REST API that returns results in pages. Every build writes exactly 100 rows, while the API holds about 40,000 records. Each response contains a field with a token for the next page. What is the most likely fix?

choices.text: Change the dataset to an incremental output, because a full rebuild keeps only the last page that the API returned during the run
Run the build with more memory, because the transform stops writing rows once its default memory limit is reached at about 100 records
Make the transform loop through the pages, requesting the next page with the token until a response comes back without a token
Ask for a higher API rate limit, because the API returns only one page per day until the account is upgraded to a paid tier

stem: In an external transform, the developer can use the HTTP client provided by the imported REST API source or bring their own Python HTTP library. What does the built-in client offer?

choices.text: It comes pre-configured with the source's details, such as its URL and certificates, so requests can start without extra setup
It runs requests on the user's own laptop, so the API sees the developer's network address rather than Foundry's during each build
It removes the need for an egress policy, because built-in client calls are treated as internal traffic between Palantir services
It caches every API response in Foundry for a day, so repeated builds never send a second request to the external system

stem: A builder creates a `Sensor Reading` object type from a dataset and proposes the reading's timestamp as the primary key, since "two readings never happen at the same time". Which choice fits the documented guidance?

choices.text: Use a Boolean valid flag as the primary key, because it is the smallest base type and keeps each object as light as possible
Use a deterministic String key from the sensor id plus the sensor's own reading sequence number; the docs discourage time keys
Keep the timestamp, because time-based types are the recommended primary key wherever events happen in a steady order over time
Use the measured value as a Double primary key, because a numeric key gives faster filtering than any text key in applications

stem: In a new app, every `Supplier` object appears under a code such as SUP-0193 in lists and search results. Users want to see the supplier's company name instead. The objects and links work correctly. What should the builder change?

choices.text: Add the company names as aliases on the object type, so that search results and lists show the alias in place of the supplier code
Make the company name the primary key, because the primary key is the value that applications show as the label of every object
Change the plural display name of the object type, which controls the label each individual object shows in lists and search results
Set the company name property as the title key of the object type, so that the name becomes the display name of each supplier object

stem: A `Depot` dataset has a latitude column and a longitude column. The team wants each depot object to carry one location value that map features can use as a geographic point. Which property base type fits?

choices.text: Geopoint, the base type for geographic points, stored as a latitude and longitude pair in one value such as 57.64,10.40
Vector, because the base types reference describes vectors as the way to place objects on maps for spatial searches
Struct, because combining latitude and longitude as two fields of one property is how the Ontology represents a location
Geoshape, because it stores any geographic feature, and a single depot is best modeled as a polygon around its site

stem: Each row of the `Shipment` dataset has a carrier code that matches the primary key of the `Carrier` object type. Each shipment has one carrier; a carrier has many shipments. How should the link type be defined?

choices.text: Without a link type, by copying every carrier property into the shipment dataset, so applications never need to traverse a link
As a foreign key link: the shipment's carrier code property refers to the carrier's primary key, giving a one-to-many relationship
As an object-backed link, because a third object type is required whenever one side of a relationship can have many linked objects
As a join table dataset link, because every link type in the Ontology needs its own dataset that lists each pair of linked objects

stem: Technicians hold many certifications, and each certification is held by many technicians. Supervisors must add and remove these pairings from an app through actions. How should the link type be backed?

choices.text: With a one-to-one link type, since the docs enforce one-to-one cardinality and that keeps each pairing unique across both object types
With two separate one-to-many link types, one per direction, because a single link type can be traversed in only one direction
With a foreign key property on the technician that stores a single certification id, updated each time a new certification is earned
With a join table dataset that lists each technician and certification pair, as the docs require for an editable many-to-many link

stem: A crew planning app links `Flight` and `Crew Member`. Planners must also record each person's role on that flight and when they were assigned, and see those details on the relationship itself. Which link design fits?

choices.text: Create one link type per role, such as Captain and First Officer links, and record the assignment date in the flight's own notes field
Store role and assignment date as two extra properties on the Crew Member object, overwritten each time the person flies again
An object-backed link: an intermediary object type, such as Crew Assignment, links both sides and carries role and assigned date
Add role and date columns to a join table dataset, because join tables show any extra columns as properties of each link

stem: A dispatcher deleted a `Vehicle` object through an action by mistake. The vehicle's row is still in the backing dataset and the dataset has been rebuilt since, yet the object stays hidden in every app. What explains this?

choices.text: The row now fails the primary key check, because a deleted key is reserved and can never again be used by any object of that type
A deletion applied through an action keeps the object hidden whatever the datasource holds; recreating it does not bring back old edits
The rebuild failed silently, because a successful build always restores every object whose row is still present in the backing data
Deleted objects stay in a recycle bin for thirty days, and the object reappears by itself once that period has passed after the deletion

stem: Dispatchers need an action to move a shipment to another carrier. The `Shipment` to `Carrier` link is a foreign key link. The builder tries a Create link rule, but it does not fit this link type. What should the action use instead?

choices.text: A Delete object rule followed by a Create object rule, so that the shipment is recreated with the new carrier inside one action
A schedule rule that rebuilds the backing dataset, because foreign key links can change only when the source dataset is rebuilt
A notification rule, because changing a link on a foreign key relationship is only possible by asking an Ontology owner to do it
A Modify object rule that sets the shipment's carrier code property, since foreign key links change by editing the foreign key

stem: Field staff will report safety incidents only through an app; no source system holds incidents. The builder creates an `Incident` object type without a backing datasource. What does the documentation require for such a type?

choices.text: Create an empty dataset by hand first, because every object type needs a backing dataset before any action is able to create objects
Skip the primary key, because objects created only through actions receive internal ids and do not need a primary key property
Save it in a project, configure an object security policy for who can view the objects, and give each new incident a unique primary key
Rely on the app's sharing settings for viewing, because objects created through actions follow the permissions of the app used

stem: An `Approve Part Order` action must succeed only when the user belongs to the maintenance planners group and the selected part's status is In stock. Users run it from Workshop, Object Explorer and Quiver. Where should the rule live?

choices.text: In the action type's submission criteria, combining a current user group condition with a condition on the part's status property
In a marking on the status property, so that only planners can see the status and therefore only planners can approve parts
In each Workshop module, by hiding the action button for users outside the group and greying it out whenever the status is wrong
In an automation that runs after each approval and reverses it when the user was not a planner or the part was not in stock

stem: To keep contractors from closing work orders, a builder adds a submission criterion that passes when the current user is not a member of the Contractors group. A reviewer flags it as a misconfiguration. Why?

choices.text: Tokens scoped to part of a user's permissions may lack the group, so the condition passes; require membership in an allowed group instead
NOT conditions slow every submission because Foundry must list all members of the group, so the action may time out for large teams
Submission criteria cannot check group membership at all; the builder must use a marking on the work order objects to block contractors
Group conditions are evaluated only once a day, so a contractor added to the group this morning could still close work orders today

stem: Planners changed a ticket's priority through an action yesterday. Today the source system sent a new priority for the same ticket, but the app still shows the planner's value. Which explanation and option are correct?

choices.text: The source value is queued behind the edit and will show after a force build, which applies all pending datasource changes at once
The nightly build failed, because a successful build always replaces every property with the values that arrive in the backing data
User edits expire after six hours, so the planner's value will disappear by itself once the next scheduled object update completes
By default user edits win over later source updates; the Apply most recent value strategy lets a newer source timestamp win instead

stem: A planner applied an action that set the wrong due date on one work order. The team asks how to undo just that one edit. What does the documentation say?

choices.text: Rebuild the backing dataset, because a rebuild replaces every user edit with the values that come from the source data
Use the drop all edits option, which removes only the latest edit on each object and keeps all older edits on the type
There is no direct undo for a single edit; apply another edit, for example the same action with the correct due date
Revert the last transaction on the object type's dataset, which removes the most recent user edit and restores the old value

stem: An analytics pipeline needs the latest state of every `Order` object, including status changes users made through actions. Reading the backing dataset misses those changes. Which source should the pipeline read?

choices.text: The action log of every action type that touches orders, replayed in the pipeline to rebuild the current status of each order
A materialized dataset of the object type, which combines the datasource values with user edits into the latest object state
A daily export of the Workshop table that users see, uploaded as a file so that the pipeline has the edited values each day
The backing dataset after a force build, since a force build writes all pending user edits back into the source data

stem: Several Workshop modules use a property of the `Asset` object type. A builder wants its name to read better for users, for example "Last service date" instead of last_svc_dt. What is the safe change?

choices.text: Rename the backing dataset column, so the property is detected again with a new ID and display name taken from the new column
Change the property ID to the new wording, because the property ID is the label users see in every application and search result
Delete the property and add a new one with the better name, then rebuild the backing dataset so values move to the new property
Change the property's display name only, because changing a saved property ID that applications reference breaks those apps

stem: A procurement director says invoices "take forever" between requisition and payment, but nobody can say where they wait. The steps already leave records in the ERP and in Foundry. Which Palantir capability is built for seeing how this purchase-to-pay process actually runs and where it gets stuck?

choices.text: Machinery, which models the process as states and transitions of the invoice entity and can mine the real flow from historical state changes
AIP Logic, which reads each invoice object with a language model and writes a short explanation of why that particular invoice has been delayed
Pipeline Builder, which joins the ERP tables into one clean dataset so that a weekly report can list every invoice that is older than thirty days
Data Connection, which syncs the ERP approval tables into Foundry on a schedule so that the finance team can open them next to the invoice records

stem: A team wants to model its parcel delivery process in Machinery. The Parcel object type has these string properties: `name`, `status` (values such as received, sorted, out for delivery, delivered), `notes` and `driver_comment`. Which property should represent the process state?

choices.text: `name`, because each parcel has its own unique name and Machinery needs one distinct value per parcel to follow it through the process
`status`, because it holds a small fixed set of values describing the parcel's current condition, which is what a state needs to be
`notes`, because staff write the parcel's progress into it in their own words, which gives the richest description of each step taken
`driver_comment`, because drivers update it at every stop, so it changes most often and best reflects the parcel's movement over time

stem: While modelling employee onboarding in Machinery, a builder finds that an employee can be "onboarded" and at the same time "awaiting payment" from payroll. Putting all of these values in one `state` property keeps breaking the graph. What does the Machinery documentation recommend?

choices.text: Drop the payroll states from the model entirely, because Machinery is only able to track a single linear process for any one object type
Let each employee hold a list of current states in one property, so that Machinery can place the same object on several nodes of the graph at once
Model onboarding and payment as separate processes, with a parent process that tracks whether the employee is ready to be paid
Combine the two values into one compound state such as "onboarded and awaiting payment", so that each employee still has only one state at a time

stem: A builder points Machinery at the Claim object type, which holds only each claim's current `state`. Mining shows the states, but the team cannot see which paths claims took or how long they spent in each state. What is missing?

choices.text: An enumeration value type on the state property, because Machinery only records transitions when the state values come from a fixed list
A Workshop module with the Machinery widget, because transitions and durations are only calculated when the graph is shown inside an app
A second process container nested inside the claim process, because transitions are stored on the child container and durations on the parent
A log object type that records each state change of a claim with its old state, new state and timestamp, which Machinery uses to derive paths

stem: A hospital's patient transfers happen in an external system that Foundry does not edit. The team wants Machinery to track how patients move between wards. What must they provide for Machinery to build the process log?

choices.text: A dataset in changelog format with one row per state change, giving the process id, the new state and the timestamp of the transition
An action type on the log object type that staff submit for every transfer, so that the log is filled in by hand as transfers occur
A daily snapshot of the ward table that overwrites each patient's current ward, so that Machinery can compare one snapshot with the next
A free-text export of the transfer system's audit messages, which Machinery reads with a language model to infer each patient's states

stem: Two teams start with Machinery. Team one has three years of state-change history for its insurance claims. Team two is designing a brand-new equipment inspection process that has no data yet. How should each team create its process model?

choices.text: Both teams should draw the model by hand first, because process mining is only used later to monitor a process that has already been drawn and published
Team one should draw by hand to avoid noise in old data, while team two should mine because a new process has no errors in it to filter out
Team one can mine the model from its historical state changes, while team two draws its states and transitions by hand from the planned design
Both teams should wait to mine, because Machinery can only build a model from historical data and cannot represent a process that has never run

stem: A team mines its order-to-cash process in Machinery. The result shows dozens of rare transitions, including a few caused by a typo in an old status value, and the graph is too tangled to discuss. What is the intended way to get a usable model?

choices.text: Accept the full mined graph as the process definition, because Machinery hides any transition that occurs in fewer than one percent of objects
Apply the transition filter to keep the most frequent share of transitions, and list the typo values as excluded elements in the mining settings
Switch mining to read only the process objects instead of the log objects, because current states alone contain fewer unusual transitions
Delete the rows with rare transitions from the source dataset, so that the next mining run only sees the common paths and produces a cleaner graph

stem: A team drew its returns process in Machinery last year, then connected real data and opened mining mode. One transition, "inspected -> refunded", appears as a dashed line. What does this tell them?

choices.text: The transition occurs in the data and already exists in the definition, so it is shown in a lighter style to distinguish it from the new findings
The transition is caused by an automation rather than a manual action, so Machinery shows it dashed to separate automated steps from human steps
The transition was found in the data for the first time and will be added to the process definition once the team confirms the mining result
The transition is in the current definition but has no reference in the data, which may indicate a problem with the drawn process definition

stem: A builder renames the state "pending_qc" to "Waiting for quality check" in a Machinery graph. Afterwards, an action's submission criteria still check for "pending_qc", and the Ontology data still shows the old value. Why?

choices.text: Changing a state in Machinery changes the model, not the Ontology data or its dependencies; to show a friendly label, set a display name
The rename failed to save, because states connected to actions are locked and can only be renamed after the actions are removed from the graph
The Ontology rejected the change, because a state can only be renamed by changing the enumeration value type that backs the state property
Machinery is waiting for the next log pipeline build, after which the data and the action's submission criteria will both use the new value

stem: A team has drawn its maintenance work-order process in Machinery. A planner asks what actually moves a work order from "scheduled" to "in progress" when that change happens inside Foundry, and how the graph reflects it. Which answer matches the Machinery documentation?

choices.text: The log object type moves it: Machinery writes the new state into the work order each time a new log entry is created for that order
The Machinery widget moves it: selecting a state node in the Workshop app moves the currently selected work orders into that state
An action moves it: the graph places that action between the states it accepts as input and the states it can produce as output
Process mining moves it: each mining run advances objects to the next state that the mined graph shows as the most frequent path

stem: A logistics manager uses the Machinery widget in a Workshop app to find shipments that sit too long in "awaiting customs". She wants the slowest ones handed to a team that can act on them. Which approach uses the widget as intended?

choices.text: Rebuild the process with a separate container for slow shipments, so that late shipments appear in their own process alongside the normal ones
Select the state and the long-duration buckets in the duration distribution, which filters the widget's output object set for the team to act on
Export the graph as an image and send it to the customs team, who then search for the slow shipments themselves in the source system
Ask an AIP Logic function to read the whole process graph and write a summary of which customs cases it considers slow and why they waited

stem: The Machinery widget shows 8,200 orders across the graph, but the order object set given to it holds 9,000 orders. The gap has stayed the same for a week, and the log object type has about 60,000 entries. A manager suspects missing data. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.text: The widget can only display the first 8,200 objects of any input set, so the remaining orders are dropped until the input is split into two parts
By default the widget shows only processes that conform to the definition, so orders that took states or transitions missing from the model are hidden
The log object type is still being indexed after a build, so the remaining orders will appear on their own within a few minutes
Orders without a link to a parent process are discarded, because the widget only counts objects that belong to a nested subprocess container

stem: An operations lead asks what AIP Logic is before approving a pilot. Which description matches Palantir's documentation?

choices.text: A no-code environment for building, testing and releasing LLM-powered functions that take inputs such as objects or text and use the Ontology
A model training service that fine-tunes a private language model on the company's Ontology so that it can answer questions without any prompts
A chat interface where any user asks free-form questions about Foundry datasets and receives answers without any function being built or released
A code repository template where engineers write Python that calls an LLM provider's API with their own keys and deploy it as a scheduled transform

stem: A builder created a Logic function that proposes a new priority for an incident object. Dispatchers should click a button in their Workshop app and have the new priority saved on the incident. Which setup does the documentation describe?

choices.text: Share the Logic file with the dispatchers, who run it in AIP Logic and copy the result into the incident by hand
Give the Logic function edit permission on the object type, so that its runs from any app change the incident immediately
Publish the Logic function, create an action backed by it, and use that action in the Workshop module
Save the Logic file in each dispatcher's home folder, so that every run happens with that dispatcher's own permissions

stem: A Logic function is meant to recommend a fix for a customer complaint based on similar past complaints, but in a test run it returns an obviously wrong recommendation. The builder wants to understand why before changing anything. Where should they look first?

choices.text: The function's usage metrics, which show success and failure counts and execution duration across all of the function's runs over the last week
The Ontology Manager page of the complaint object type, which lists every property the language model read during the run and its values
The raw source dataset behind the complaint objects, because a wrong answer from a Logic function almost always comes from bad source data
The Debugger for that run, which shows the model's chain of thought for each block, the generated prompts and the tools it called

stem: A Logic function has an input `customer` (a Customer object) and a Use LLM block whose prompt says "Write a renewal reminder that fits this customer's contract". The drafts are generic and never mention the contract end date stored on the object. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The prompt is too short, so the builder should add several paragraphs of general guidance about how a good renewal reminder is written
The prompt never inserts the customer's properties, and the model only sees what the prompt explicitly gives it, so it cannot know the date
The function needs a Query objects tool for every object type in the Ontology, so that the model can search for the contract on its own
The model in the block is too small to read contract data, so the builder should switch to the largest model available in the platform

stem: A Logic function drafts a quote for a customer and must include the total price, which comes from quantities, unit prices and a discount. In tests, the language model sometimes adds the numbers up wrongly. Which built-in option does AIP Logic offer for this?

choices.text: Give the Use LLM block the Calculator tool, which lets the model perform accurate mathematical calculations instead of estimating them
Lower the number of line items per quote, because language models are only unreliable at arithmetic when the list of numbers is long
Replace the language model with a newer one for every quote, because newer models are guaranteed to calculate prices without mistakes
Ask the model in the prompt to double-check its arithmetic twice and to state each intermediate sum before writing the final quote

stem: A team already has a tested TypeScript function that computes a supplier's risk score. Their new Logic function needs that score before the language model drafts a supplier review. What is the simplest approach?

choices.text: Rewrite the scoring logic as a chain of Create variable blocks inside the Logic function so that everything lives in one place
Paste the scoring rules into the prompt and ask the language model to compute the risk score itself before drafting the review
Call the existing function with an Execute function block and pass its output to the Use LLM block that drafts the review
Export the risk scores to a spreadsheet each night and attach the file to the prompt, so that the model can look up each score

stem: A Logic function always sets an incident's priority to "high" when its severity property is critical. The team wants this step to fill the action parameters the same way every time and run fast. Which building block fits best?

choices.text: A Query objects tool that lets the model read the incident's severity and decide for itself whether the priority needs changing
An Apply actions tool in a Use LLM block, with a prompt telling the model to set high priority whenever the incident looks critical
A Call function tool that hands the incident to another Logic function, which then asks a second language model to set the priority
An Apply action block, which calls the action deterministically with parameters the builder fills in, without going through an LLM

stem: A Logic function that triages supplier emails has been published for a month and is used by many people. The team lead wants to know whether it has started failing more often and running slower over the last two weeks, across everyone's runs. Where should the lead look?

choices.text: The Debugger of a test run started now, because its chain of thought for each block shows how fast and how reliably the function has worked lately
The lead's own recent runs in the Run panel, because each user can open every execution log of the function there in the default execution mode
A Machinery graph of the email object type, because process mining measures how long each published function takes and how often it fails
The function's monitoring metrics, which track success and failure counts and execution duration of the function over time across its runs

stem: A builder backs a Workshop Markdown widget with a Logic function so that it shows a short case summary. The widget cannot use the function, which currently returns a Case object with an updated summary property. What does the documentation require?

choices.text: The Logic function must take no inputs at all, because Markdown widgets cannot pass objects from the module to a function
The Logic function must return a string for a Markdown widget, so the output should be the summary text itself
The Logic function must run in project-scoped mode, because Markdown widgets cannot call functions run with user permissions
The Logic function must apply an Ontology edit through an action, because Markdown widgets only display saved properties

stem: Three analysts share a Logic function. Each can see only their own runs in the execution logs, which makes it hard to investigate each other's failures. The project's members are all allowed to see these runs. Which setting explains this and what changes it?

choices.text: Logs of other users are visible only to platform administrators, so the team must file a request each time it needs a colleague's run
Logs are tied to the analyst who created the Logic file, so its ownership should move to a shared service account to make them visible
It runs in the default user-scoped mode; project-scoped mode uses project permissions and shows the logs to all project members
Logs stay private for the first week after each publish, so the team should wait until the current version has been in use for longer

stem: A Logic function has a Query objects tool on the Employee object type. A user without access to salary data runs it, and a manager worries that the model could read salaries through the tool. In user-scoped mode, what does the documentation say?

choices.text: The model only asks to use tools; AIP Logic runs the calls within the invoking user's permissions, so it cannot read data the user cannot read
The model receives all Employee properties because the tool was configured by the builder, whose permissions apply to every later run
The model calls tools with the function's own service identity, so the manager is right and salaries must be removed from the Ontology
The model can read salaries but is told in the prompt to ignore them, which is how AIP Logic keeps restricted fields out of its answers

stem: A Logic function reads restricted HR case details for an authorized user and writes a summary into a property of a widely shared Case object. The security lead notes that restricted views protected the source rows. What does the documentation advise?

choices.text: Disable the function's Use LLM block for HR data, because AIP Logic cannot be used on any object type that has row-level access controls
Ask the model in the prompt never to repeat sensitive details, because prompt instructions are the documented control for model outputs
Nothing more is needed, because row and column controls that applied when the model read the data also restrict everything the model writes
Pair the read-time controls with a marking or classification-based control, because they do not extend to the model's output or the edits it makes

stem: A Logic function used by a live Workshop app needs a reworked prompt and a new block. The builder wants to try the change against the app without disturbing current users. Which approach does the documentation support?

choices.text: Develop the change on a Foundry branch, test it in branch-aware apps such as Workshop, and merge it through an approved proposal
Duplicate the Logic file under a new name, point a copy of the Workshop app at it, and delete the original once the copy looks right
Describe the change in a ticket and wait for the next platform release, because Logic functions can only change when Foundry is upgraded
Edit the live function directly during a quiet hour, since users are unlikely to run it then and any problem can be undone afterwards

stem: When dispatchers open the inbox, the details panel beside the shipment table already shows the first shipment, and some act on it believing they picked it. The builder wants the panel empty until a dispatcher clicks a row. What should change?

choices.text: Turn on auto-refresh for the module, because every refresh clears the active object and leaves the details panel empty once again
Turn off the table's active object auto-selection, so the active object variable starts empty and the panel fills only after a row is clicked
Sort the table so the oldest late shipment comes first, because the panel then shows the shipment that dispatchers would pick anyway
Enable multi-select on the table, because the details panel then waits until a dispatcher has ticked at least one row before it shows data

stem: A builder sketches a dispatch app and wants to name the four Workshop core concepts correctly in the design notes. Which pairing of concept and job is correct?

choices.text: Widgets store data between user sessions, variables decide the screen arrangement, events hold filter values, and layouts run the writeback Actions
Widgets define the object types, variables grant users access, events schedule data refreshes, and layouts calculate aggregations over object sets
Widgets display content, variables carry data between widgets, events trigger behavior when users act, and layouts organize the header, pages and sections
Widgets trigger the pipeline builds, variables are the dataset columns, events record user activity for audits, and layouts set module permissions

stem: A builder adds a Filter List beside an Object Table of shipments. Users pick a status in the filter, but the table keeps showing every shipment. Both widgets use the Shipment object type. What is the most likely gap?

choices.text: The object type needs a new pipeline build after each filter choice before the table is able to show the filtered set of shipments
The Filter List's filter output was never applied to the object set that backs the table, so the table still reads the unfiltered set
Filters only take effect once a user saves a state of the module, so the table changes after the user saves and reopens that state
Filter List widgets only affect chart widgets, so the table has to be replaced with a chart before any user filter can take effect

stem: A builder backed a Filter List with the same filtered object set variable that feeds the shipments table. After a user filters to "Late", the filter itself only offers "Late" and users cannot widen it again. What should change?

choices.text: Add a second Object Table that always shows every shipment so users can copy the status they need back into the filter by hand
Ask the ontology owner to split the Shipment object type into one object type per status so that each status gets its own table
Replace the Filter List with a String Selector widget, because Filter List widgets cannot be used together with an Object Table widget
Back the Filter List with its own unfiltered object set of shipments and apply its filter output only to the object set behind the table

stem: Dispatchers want to tick several late shipments in a table and reassign them together with one Action that accepts a list of shipments. Today the Action form only ever receives the highlighted row. What should the builder change?

choices.text: Copy the table into a Loop layout so the Action runs once for every object shown in the loop when the dispatcher submits the form
Add one Button Group per shipment row so that each dispatcher clicks one button for every shipment that needs to be reassigned
Enable multi-select on the table and default the Action's shipment parameter to the table's Selected objects output variable
Ask the ontology owner to add a new Selected property to Shipment that dispatchers set by hand before they run the Action

stem: A builder exposes a Reassign Shipment Action on a button and asks whether they now have to design the input form (fields, validation, submit) as a separate set of widgets. What do the docs say?

choices.text: No, a form is generated automatically from the Action definition, and the builder only sets defaults and visibility for its parameters
Yes, the form has to be built in a separate forms tool, and Workshop can only link to it from a button that opens a new browser tab
No, Workshop writes the user's edits directly into the backing dataset, so no form or Action is involved when a dispatcher saves a change
Yes, every field must be built as Text Input and Date Input widgets, and a Function then copies their values into the Ontology on submit

stem: When a dispatcher clicks Reassign on the shipment they are viewing, the Action form asks them to pick the same shipment again from a long list. How should the builder configure the button?

choices.text: Set the shipment parameter's default to the table's Active object variable and mark that parameter Hidden in the Action form
Mark the shipment parameter Disabled with no default value, so dispatchers cannot change it and the form submits whatever shipment is open
Remove the shipment parameter from the action type, so the Action guesses which shipment is meant from the dispatcher's last click
Leave the shipment parameter with no default, and add a description to the button that reminds dispatchers to search for the right shipment first

stem: A dispatcher fills in a Reassign form, but the submit control stays unavailable and the form flags one issue on the new depot code they typed. Other dispatchers submit the same Action without trouble. What is happening?

choices.text: The Shipment object type is out of date, and the form blocks submission until the next pipeline build of the backing dataset finishes
The dispatcher lacks the Editor role on the Workshop module, and the form blocks submission for anyone who cannot edit the module itself
The module has unpublished changes, and the form blocks submission until the builder publishes a new version of the module for everyone
The value fails the action type's submission criteria, so the form blocks submission until the dispatcher enters a code that passes

stem: A planner can open the dispatch module and use it, but cannot change its layout when asked to help add a new page. What is the most likely reason?

choices.text: The module has never been published; until the first publish, only the person who created it is technically able to edit its layout
The planner holds only the Viewer role on the module; opening needs Viewer by default, while editing the module needs the Editor role
The planner is missing a role on the Shipment object type; editing a module's layout needs Owner on every object type it displays
The planner is not in the group that may configure action types, and only members of that group are allowed to change any module layout

stem: A builder created the first dispatch module in a personal sandbox folder and sent dispatchers the link. Dispatchers cannot open it, although they hold Viewer on the dispatch team's project. What fits best?

choices.text: Publish the module once more, because a published module is open to every user in the organization regardless of where it is saved
Add the dispatchers' names to the module header, because the header list decides which users may open the module in view mode
Save the module in the dispatch team's project, since a module inherits the permissions of the project or folder it is created in
Give each dispatcher the Editor role on the sandbox folder, so they can open the module and also adjust it for their own needs

stem: Two dispatchers from different regions open the same module at the same moment and see different shipments in the same table. The builder suspects a bug in the filter setup. What is the more likely explanation?

choices.text: Row-level controls such as object security policies filter what each user may read, and Workshop widgets never show data a user cannot read
Each browser keeps its own cached copy of the data, and the copies drift apart until both dispatchers clear the cache and reload the module
Auto-refresh is off for one of the users, so that user sees an older set of shipments until a scheduled pipeline build runs again
The module interface variables differ between the two links, and module interface variables always restrict data by the user's region

stem: Dispatchers need a short handover checklist for the selected shipment now and then, without losing their place in the shipment list. Which design fits Workshop guidance best?

choices.text: Put the checklist on a second page and use a Switch to page event, so the dispatchers leave the shipment list each time they need it
Add the checklist permanently to the main page next to the table, so it is always visible to every dispatcher whether it is needed or not
Put the checklist in a drawer overlay that a button opens with a Layers event, shown on top of the page the dispatcher is working on
Build the checklist as a separate module and send dispatchers its link, so they open it in another browser tab whenever it is needed

stem: The dispatch app now has three distinct workflows: an inbox of late shipments, a depot overview and a weekly report. Users must always see navigation between them. Which layout fits?

choices.text: Build three separate modules with no links between them, and ask users to keep a bookmark for each one in their browser toolbar
Put each workflow on its own page and add a Tabs widget to the module header, since the header persists across every page
Put all three workflows into one long Flow section so that users scroll down the page to reach the depot overview and then the weekly report
Use one page and stack the three workflows in collapsible sections, so users expand the one they need and collapse the other two

stem: Fleet managers want one small card per truck in a set of 20 to 40 trucks, each card showing the same few fields and a button. The number of trucks changes daily. Which Workshop layout fits?

choices.text: Copy one configured card section 40 times and hide the extra copies on days when fewer trucks are in the set the managers are viewing
Use a Flow layout, which turns any object set into one generated card per object without needing any embedded module at all
Use a Tabs layout with one tab per truck, adding or removing tabs by hand each morning to match the trucks that are in service
Use a Loop layout over the truck object set, displaying an embedded module for each object in the set as a repeated card

stem: The operations lead wants a large number at the top of the inbox that shows how many shipments are currently late, updating as the data changes. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: A static numeric variable that the operations lead updates by hand each morning, displayed in a Text widget at the top of the inbox
An Object Table of late shipments with a count column added to every row, so that users can read the total from the first row
A Function that writes the count into a new Shipment property each night, displayed in an Object View widget at the top of the page
A numeric variable defined as an object set aggregation (count) over the late shipments set, displayed in a Metric Card widget

stem: A builder wants a warehouse table to show each warehouse's number of open shipments, through the one-to-many Warehouse-to-Shipment link, without changing the Ontology for this one app. Which option fits best?

choices.text: Add a Workshop derived property on Warehouse that counts linked open shipments; it is computed at query time and exists only in that module
Ask the ontology owner to add an Open Shipment Count property to the Warehouse object type and change the pipeline to compute it
Export the shipments table to a spreadsheet each day, count shipments per warehouse there, and upload the counts as a new dataset
Add a static numeric variable per warehouse and ask a supervisor to type in each warehouse's current count after every shift ends

stem: A supervisor filters the inbox to unresolved shipments at one depot, selects a shipment, and wants to keep that exact view to return to later and to share with a coworker. Which Workshop feature is designed for this?

choices.text: An embedded module per supervisor, which keeps a private copy of each user's filters inside the parent module until they are cleared
State saving, with the filter and selection variables enabled for it, so the supervisor saves the view and can share the saved state
Routing for the Filter List's filter variable, which writes that object set filter variable into the URL as a query parameter to share
Auto-refresh, which stores the supervisor's current filters on the server and restores them each time the module reloads for anyone

stem: After state saving was enabled for the inbox filters, a dispatcher complains that the module opens with default filters every morning instead of yesterday's choices. What explains this?

choices.text: The Filter List's external ID changes every night, so every saved filter is erased overnight and has to be recreated each morning
State saving only applies in edit mode, so dispatchers in view mode never get their filters restored when they open the module again
State saving does not persist values automatically; the dispatcher must explicitly save a state and later open that saved state
The module must also have auto-refresh enabled, because auto-refresh is the feature that restores each user's last filter values

stem: An alert email should contain a link that opens the shipment inbox with one specific shipment already selected. How is this done in Workshop?

choices.text: Make the selected-shipment variable part of the module interface with an external ID, and pass the shipment's ID as a URL parameter
Copy the module's edit-mode URL while that shipment is selected, because the edit-mode address stores the builder's current selection
Duplicate the inbox module once per shipment and link each email to the copy that was built for that particular shipment's alert
Create one saved state for every shipment ahead of time and put the matching saved state into each alert email when it is sent out

stem: A "shipment card" module is embedded in three dispatch modules. The builder edits and saves the card module, but none of the three parent modules shows the change. What is the most likely reason?

choices.text: Embedding is only refreshed by the auto-refresh feature, so parents show child changes after the next data change in the object set
Embedded modules are copied into the parent when first added, so the parent modules must remove the card and add it back to get updates
An embedded module always runs in its published version, and the builder saved the card module without publishing the new version
The parents still map old interface variables, and any change in a child module is ignored until every parent adds a new variable

stem: After auto-refresh worked well on the operations wall display, a builder proposes turning it on in every module, including a monthly cost report that nobody watches live. What is the better position?

choices.text: Turn it off everywhere, because auto-refresh only works in edit mode and cannot keep the operations wall display current for viewers
Turn it on everywhere, because auto-refresh has no cost and reloads only the single widget whose data has changed since the last refresh
Turn it on everywhere, because without auto-refresh users never see any new data in a module, even after they reload the page themselves
Turn it on only where freshness matters, because auto-refresh can raise data load and cost and reloads all data in the module on updates

stem: After a dispatcher successfully submits Reassign Shipment from a button on the details page, the app should take them back to the inbox page. What fits Workshop?

choices.text: Chain a Switch to page event on the button with the trigger set to run on start of the Action submission, before it is processed
Chain a Switch to page event on the button with the trigger set to run on successful completion of the Action submission
Add a second button labelled Back that dispatchers click after the toast appears, which runs a Switch to page event to the inbox page
Turn on auto-refresh for the module, which returns users to the inbox page whenever an Action edits an object they are viewing

stem: A team found a polished alert inbox in the Workshop Design Hub and started editing it in place to fit their shipments. Their edits are blocked, and a colleague warns that edits there could be lost anyway. What should they do?

choices.text: Ask an administrator to make the Design Hub project read-write, and then continue editing the example inbox module in its current place
Rebuild the inbox from scratch without looking at the example, because Design Hub modules cannot be copied into any other project
Duplicate the example module into their own project and adapt the copy, treating the Design Hub modules as read-only inspiration
Embed the Design Hub inbox into an empty module and edit the embedded child module in place, since embedding unlocks editing

stem: The first dispatch app grew to about 25 visible widgets on one page and nine buttons in the top navigation. Users say they cannot find what to do next. Which redesign follows the Workshop design guidance?

choices.text: Keep every widget but shrink them all to fit one screen, so that users never have to scroll and can see every element at the same time
Move every widget into modal overlays opened from the top navigation, so the main page stays empty until a user asks for something
Add a help page that lists all 25 widgets and nine buttons with a short description, and link that page from the top of the module
Cut each view to about ten visible components and at most five primary actions in the top navigation, surfacing the rest when needed

stem: Dispatchers want to correct a few delay reasons quickly in the shipment table instead of opening a form for every row. A builder wonders whether inline editing bypasses the governed writeback path. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Inline editing writes each changed cell straight into the backing dataset, so it skips the Action and its submission criteria entirely
Inline editing in the Object Table is defined through an Action configured in the Ontology, so cell edits still go through that Action
Inline editing is available only to users with Owner on the object type, because it bypasses the permissions that Actions check
Inline editing only changes what the current user sees in the table, so the edits are never saved to objects and vanish on reload
